why: The other half of the gameplay-entry exemption, one level down: the runner honours the caller's `instant` rather than consulting the configured duration. Mutated here the flag still threads through every call site and still typechecks, so `transition-runs-on-gameplay-entry` above -- which pins the ARGUMENT -- cannot see it, and neither can transitions.test.ts, which never passes `instant` (0 call sites, checked). `instant` is a property of WHICH change this is, not of how long transitions happen to be configured to take, so a build that merely set the duration low would not restore the guarantee. `never runs a transition on gameplay entry` is again the case that measures it, through hud.ts's two `showCustomize(false, true)` / `showControllers(false, true)` cleanup closes and setState's own call. Scoped to hud.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only. The killer's NAME changed in issue #323, not its subject: the case still sweeps the non-paused states for this button, but the Main Menu is now the only one that withholds it, so the title says that instead.
